% Fixture: failures/warn-duplicate-label
%
% Purpose: verify that multiply-defined labels produce warnings.
%
% Expected maketex behaviour:
%   - Engine: pdflatex
%   - Passes: 2 (first pass triggers "Label(s) may have changed. Rerun…")
%   - Exit: 0 (success — LaTeX does not treat this as fatal)
%   - PDF produced (second reference wins; output is unpredictable)
%
% Log warnings (after second pass, exact text):
%   LaTeX Warning: Label `sec:duplicate' multiply defined.
%   LaTeX Warning: There were multiply-defined labels.
%
% The error surfacing system should:
%   - classify these as warnings
%   - extract the label key "sec:duplicate" from the message
%   - surface them after the build completes
%
% Note: the first pass emits "Label(s) may have changed. Rerun to get
% cross-references right." which drives the second pass; the multiply-defined
% warning only appears on the second pass.

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

\section{First Section}
\label{sec:duplicate}

This is the first section with label \texttt{sec:duplicate}.

\section{Second Section}
\label{sec:duplicate}

This section accidentally reuses the same label.
The cross-reference \ref{sec:duplicate} is now ambiguous.

\end{document}
